thesis: A pursuit map separates competence from energy when evaluating activities.
summary: The reviewed passages introduce a two-axis map and identify high competence with low energy as a potential trap. The source suggests modifying draining work and maintaining room for activities that generate interest even before proficiency develops. These are reflection prompts, not validated assessments or guarantees against burnout. The selected passages do not capture every rule described in the video.

insights.title: Assess energy separately from ability
insights.explanation: The framework warns that being good at an activity does not by itself establish that it is sustainable or fulfilling.
insights.quote: the zone of danger high competency but low energy
insights.speaker: unresolved

insights.title: Try adjusting one draining activity
insights.explanation: The proposed exercise begins with a specific activity and asks how its design might change, rather than immediately requiring a complete career exit.
insights.quote: choose one item in this zone and think about how you might be able to adjust it

insights.title: Maintain room for energizing beginner activities
insights.explanation: The creator treats interest as a reason to explore while skill develops. This is about personal exploration, not proof of market demand.
